messages.author: c842d5c60a247e87
messages.subject: Re: Strange output CFI = 1 and RMSA = 0.000
parts:
Hi Daniel,

People more experienced than me with Lavaan and SEM might be better placed to provide you with an answer but my take is that as you are using what seems to be a saturated model in which measurement error is absent (you don't specify any latent variable) your model fits the data perfectly, hence fit indices are perfect (the implied covariance matrix of your model matches the actual data covariance matrix). In other words, I don't think there is anything wrong here... But it will be informative to read others' answers.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Strange output CFI = 1 and RMSA = 0.000
parts: People more experienced than me with Lavaan and SEM might be better placed to provide you with an answer but my take is that as you are using what seems to be a saturated model

That is correct.  You are not placing any restrictions on what your (co)variances could be.  You are not required to, but if you do have hypothesized restrictions to impose, you will have a basis to test the fit of your theoretical model to the data.  Otherwise, you can only interpret your estimated parameters.
